text:
alex: quick check-in — proposal to add a small adapter layer so org-scoped API keys can mint short-lived project-scoped tokens. aim is to avoid a big rekey for customers during the project-scoped RBAC rollout. thoughts?

maria: sounds pragmatic. main concerns: auditability and impersonation surface. adapter must stamp original principal into the minted token claims.

sam: agree. we also need to ensure adapter enforces existing org-level ACLs during mint to avoid privilege escalation.

leigh: +1. implementation detail: do we make the adapter stateful (mapping table) or stateless (signed mapping rules)? stateless is easier ops-wise but harder for revocation.

alex: revocation is the tricky bit. proposal: minted tokens are short TTL (5m) and we implement a revocation cache in the adapter that can be updated via pub/sub. revocation check on adapter mint/refresh.

maria: 5m seems ok for most flows, but background jobs that use long-lived creds will need a migration path. we should provide a compatibility CLI to rotate long-lived keys into service identities.

sam: telemetry request: emit metric `auth.adapter.mints` with labels {outcome,origin_key_type,customer_tier}. also log original key id in audit (redacted) and minted token id.

infra-bot: deploy-check: we need canary in 2 regions, rate-limit at 200rps per adapter instance, and a circuit-breaker that falls back to legacy validation if adapter misbehaves.

leigh: fallback to legacy validation is fine but be explicit about semantics: when fallback occurs, downstream sees org-scoped token semantics. that can widen access compared to project tokens if we don't transform claims. need a safe-mode.

alex: safe-mode idea: when adapter falls back, it should attach `x-auth-mode:legacy-fallback` header and write an event to `auth.fallbacks` stream. ops can alert on that.

maria: permission mapping: define deterministic rule `org:key -> project:role` for each customer. keep rules in owner-managed YAMLs stored in S3 + signed by admin key. adapter verifies signature before applying mapping.

sam: can we auto-generate mappings during onboarding via heuristics? e.g., map org-admin -> project-admin, org-service -> project-service minimal. but require manual approval before enabling for production.

leigh: API surface sketch: `POST /v1/adapter/mint` with body { "org_key": "k_XXX", "scope_hint": "project:abc" } returns { "token": "t_YYY", "ttl":300, "mapped_roles": ["writer"] }. include `audit_id` header.

alex: migration plan: 1) deploy adapter behind feature flag for internal infra. 2) telemetry-only mode where adapter simulates mint and logs diffs. 3) opt-in beta for select customers. 4) global rollout + deprecation schedule for org-scoped keys (18 months).

maria: + timeline. also need docs + SDK helpers (`rw-auth migrate-key --from org_key --to service-id`) and migration runbook.

sam: security review checklist: threat model for impersonation, replay, MITM, signing key protection, and revocation windows. also pen-test before public rollout.

ops: for rollout, recommend per-customer feature flag gating and a hard quota on mint rate. we should also ensure billing tags survive mapping.

alex: edge-case: cross-project routing — what if an org-key historically used across projects A and B? mapping needs to allow multi-project scopes or require customers split keys. prefer multi-project mapping for compatibility but warn about blast radius.

leigh: propose mapping grammar: allow `projects: [a,b]` with per-project role overrides. adapter must expand into per-project tokens or a batched token set. prefer per-project tokens for least privilege.

maria: one more: audit trail must reconstruct original request chain: org_key -> adapter_mint -> project_token -> downstream call. add unique `audit_id` UUID to all logs.

alex: thanks — I'll draft a short RFC with the API shape, TTLs, revocation design, and rollout steps. request volunteers for review: @maria, @sam, @leigh, and @ops to sanity-check the runbook.

sam: I'll take the threat model section.

maria: I'll draft the mapping grammar and signed YAML format.

infra-bot: noted: created RFC draft #1798 and assigned reviewers.

ops: happy to review rollout and telemetry playbooks.

alex: cool — meeting Friday 10am to align on open questions (revocation TTL vs usability, fallback semantics). ping me if you want to add anything before then. :thumbsup:
